column8: OBJECT size recovery after migration: every replica must report non-negative ObjectSize equal to its physical .bin bytes, including after a cache-less restart (TDB-835 regression guard)

Snapshot/GC race: a newly added replica must not keep OBJECT files the leader already physically deleted (TDB-861). The window is armed deterministically (OBJECT overwrite churn + MIGRATE REGION), see references/known-defects.md
Remove a healthy Running DataNode under read/write load (tc110).
Stop the DataNode process first, then remove it while Unknown (tc109).
Switch the DataNode to ReadOnly live, then remove it (tc111).
Remove the DataNode with data_replication_factor=1 (tc105).
Remove a DataNode id that does not exist plus malformed remove SQL (tc104).
Remove three DataNodes one after another (tc112).
Two REMOVE DATANODE procedures submitted at the same time (tc116).
kill -9 the DataNode that is being removed (tc118).
kill -9 a second DataNode while the first one is being removed.
Restart a DataNode in the middle of the remove procedure (tc13).
Re-submit REMOVE DATANODE for the same node while it runs.
Join the held-back DataNode, then remove that just-added node (grow-then-shrink; no spare host needed).
Remove DataNodes until only data_replication_factor remain; the next remove must be refused (tc117).
Issue LOAD BALANCE while the remove procedure is running (tc38).
Remove a Running DataNode while a second DataNode turns ReadOnly (tc113).
Remove a Running DataNode while a second replica goes Unknown (tc114/tc115).
Remove a Running DataNode while a second DataNode is disk-full (tc120).
Remove a Running Follower ConfigNode (tc202/tc2).
Remove the ConfigNode that currently is the Leader (tc202/tc3).
Stop a ConfigNode process, then remove it (tc201).
Remove a ConfigNode id that does not exist plus malformed remove SQL (tc202).

kill -9 another ConfigNode while the Leader is being removed. NOTE: the errors observed on this case end BEFORE the kill -9 is injected, so they come from the removal itself, not from the kill; they are part of the ConfigNode-removal transient tracked as finding 1, with every ConfigNode alive.

Restart a ConfigNode during the Follower remove procedure. NOTE: on 3 ConfigNodes this removes one (3C->2C) and then stops another, leaving 1 vote where 2 are needed, so an outage is EXPECTED here and is not an availability defect (R&D confirmed: at 2 ConfigNodes a restart cannot be made highly available). Use >=5 ConfigNodes to exercise the real high-availability path. See CN_BELOW_QUORUM_EXPECTED_OUTAGE.

Shrink the ConfigNodes one at a time down to a single node, probing after EVERY removal that the cluster can still perform a schema mutation. A one-member ConfigRegion is a valid group, so the cluster is expected to keep serving; this is NOT expected to be refused. On rc2 0b4dc9a it breaks after the second removal with 'The consensus group ConfigRegion[0] doesn't exist'.

Same shrink to a single ConfigNode, but the Leader is removed FIRST (while three still exist) and a Follower last. Companion to cn_remove_below_quorum, which removes the Leader last; together they isolate whether the outage comes from removing the Leader at size 2 or merely from reaching a single-member ConfigRegion.
Restart the same DataNode repeatedly across the remove procedure (widens the member-replacement window; the silent row loss needs a restart while the new replica is still catching up)
Restart EVERY other DataNode once during the remove procedure (ABNORMAL_DN_ROTATE=true): the node holding the freshly migrated replica is restarted by construction, instead of one node three times
TDB-116: cross-partition writes must survive a concurrent node/region removal (moved from iotdb-crud)
Big OBJECT: write ~4 GiB of OBJECT payloads in segments, then migrate every data region and verify byte-identical content (sha256 per row) plus replica sizes (OBJECT 单点上限 4 GiB 的应用场景)
TDB-861 with ~1e5 small OBJECT files: DELETE the table, then migrate every region while the old SnapshotTaker copies the whole object directory

One 4 GiB OBJECT point: write it in 8 MiB to_object(isEOF, offset, X'..') chunks (512 statements), read it back as 16 x 256 MiB ranged read_object(o, offset, length) slices with length()+sha256() compared per chunk, migrate the region and re-verify the same 16 chunks plus the .bin size on every replica
